name: Steamed Dhokla Fingers
why: Soft, spongy Gujarati snack that toddlers can pick up as finger food.
steps: Make dhokla batter with besan and curd. Steam until set. Cut into small fingers. Serve with plain curd — skip green chilli tempering for babies.

name: Soft Thepla Roll
why: Travel-friendly Gujarati flatbread that stays soft and is easy to roll.
cheese: Optional tiny grated cheese — mashed potato stuffing works well.
steps: Make thin soft theplas with methi or plain. Spread mashed potato and roll into a log. Cut into bite-sized rounds.

name: Handvo Fingers
why: Hidden vegetables in a soft baked Gujarati cake — good for picky eaters.
steps: Mix soaked rice-dal batter with grated lauki. Bake in a tray until golden and set. Cut into finger strips.

name: Khandvi Spirals
why: Soft, protein-rich Gujarati snack with a melt-in-mouth texture.
steps: Cook besan-curd mixture until thick. Spread thin on a greased surface. Roll into spirals when warm. Use very mild tempering.

name: Rajgira Banana Porridge
why: Iron and calcium from rajgira with natural sweetness from banana.
steps: Cook rajgira flour with water until smooth. Mash in ripe banana and a drop of ghee. Serve warm.

name: Quinoa Veg Khichdi
why: Complete protein from quinoa in a familiar khichdi format.
steps: Pressure-cook quinoa with moong dal and finely chopped carrot and lauki. Mash lightly and add ghee.

name: Tofu Vegetable Mash
why: Plant protein option for vegetarian families wanting soy variety.
steps: Steam carrot and pumpkin until soft. Mash with silken tofu and a little ghee. Serve with soft rice.

name: Avocado Banana Mash
why: Healthy fats plus natural sweetness — great for brain development.
steps: Mash equal parts ripe avocado and banana. Thin with breast milk or formula if needed. Serve immediately.

name: Broccoli Cheese Mash
why: Hides broccoli in a creamy paneer mash toddlers often accept.
cheese: Use crumbled paneer instead of processed cheese for better nutrition.
steps: Steam broccoli until very soft. Mash with crumbled paneer and ghee. Serve as a side with khichdi.

name: Ragi Idli with Sambar
why: Iron-rich idli paired with familiar South Indian sambar.
steps: Steam ragi idlis until soft. Serve with thin mild sambar. Cut idli into strips for self-feeding.

name: Wheat Dalia Kheer
why: Comforting warm breakfast with fibre and calcium.
steps: Cook broken wheat in milk until creamy. Sweeten naturally with mashed banana. Add a pinch of cardamom if tolerated.

name: Beetroot Oats Porridge
why: Naturally pink porridge that appeals visually without artificial colour.
steps: Cook oats with grated beetroot and water until smooth. Add ghee and serve warm.

name: Mild Fish Curry with Rice
why: Omega-3 rich meal for non-vegetarian toddlers who accept fish.
steps: Cook boneless fish in mild tomato-coconut gravy. Flake carefully. Serve over soft mashed rice.

name: Chicken Veg Soup Bowl
why: Light, nourishing soup when appetite is low or during illness recovery.
steps: Pressure-cook chicken with carrot and bottle gourd. Shred chicken finely. Serve broth with soft rice or as a drink.

name: Soft Keema with Roti
why: Iron-rich minced meat for older toddlers on non-veg diets.
steps: Slow-cook keema with grated lauki until very soft. Serve with torn soft roti pieces.

name: Sprouted Moong Chaat
why: Fresh, crunchy-soft chaat that introduces sprouts in a familiar format.
steps: Steam sprouts until soft. Mix with grated carrot and a spoon of curd. Skip chaat masala for toddlers.

name: Pea Potato Patties
why: Mild patties that work as finger food or a light dinner.
cheese: Optional tiny paneer crumble inside for extra protein.
steps: Shape mashed pea-potato mix into small patties. Pan-fry lightly in ghee until golden. Cool before serving.

name: Makhana Milk Porridge
why: Light evening snack that is easy on digestion.
steps: Grind roasted makhana to powder. Cook with milk until creamy. Sweeten with mashed banana if desired.

name: Mild Sabudana Khichdi
why: Fasting favourite adapted as a soft, energy-dense toddler meal.
steps: Soak sabudana 4 hours. Cook with boiled potato and minimal peanut (if already introduced). Keep very soft.

name: Cabbage Coconut Poriyal
why: South Indian side dish with mild coconut flavour toddlers often like.
steps: Finely shred cabbage and steam until soft. Sauté with curry leaves, a pinch of turmeric, and fresh coconut.

name: Paneer Bhurji Paratha
why: Quick protein-packed dinner using pantry staples.
cheese: Paneer is the main dairy — skip extra cheese.
steps: Make soft paneer bhurji with grated carrot. Stuff lightly in paratha or serve as a side with torn roti.

name: First Moong Dal Water
why: Classic first protein introduction for 6-month-old babies starting solids.
steps: Boil moong dal with extra water. Strain the thin dal water for first tastes. Progress to thicker soup with ghee.

name: Homemade Rice Cereal Bowl
why: Simple first food made at home without packaged cereal.
steps: Grind rice to fine powder. Cook with water to smooth porridge. Add mashed banana and a drop of ghee.

name: Zucchini Hidden Dal
why: Mild zucchini blends into dal for hidden vegetable nutrition.
steps: Steam and mash zucchini into cooked moong dal. Serve over soft rice with ghee.

name: Drumstick Sambar Idli
why: South Indian staple adapted for toddlers with thin mild sambar.
steps: Steam soft idlis. Prepare thin sambar with drumstick and carrot. Remove fibrous drumstick pieces before serving.
